stops.note: to sing a magic spell over, to bewitch, from in- and cantare
stops.meaning: to sing a magic spell over, to bewitch

stops.note: carried into French for casting a magic spell, or delighting someone greatly
stops.meaning: to cast a magic spell, or to delight someone greatly

stops.note: settled as the English word for delighting someone completely, as if by magic
stops.meaning: to delight someone completely, as if by magic

current_meaning: to fill someone with great delight, or to put a magic spell on them
